<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revolving Credit
Facility</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005, the Company had
a five-year multi-currency revolving credit facility (&#147;Revolving Credit
Facility&#148;) in the amount of $600&nbsp;million, which expires on April&nbsp;27,
2010. The Revolving Credit Facility entered into on April&nbsp;27, 2005,
replaced the Company&#146;s previously existing term loan and revolving credit
facility discussed below. The applicable margins and fees under the Revolving
Credit Facility are determined using the debt ratings issued by third party
rating agencies. Based upon current third party debt ratings, the interest rate
on U.S. dollar denominated borrowings under the Revolving Credit Facility is
LIBOR plus 0.40% or a Base Rate as defined in the agreement. The
weighted-average interest rates on outstanding borrowings were 5.8% and 5.2% at
December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005, respectively. However, $200&nbsp;million of
the Company&#146;s borrowings under this facility was hedged by using interest rate
derivative agreements. This resulted in an average effective interest rate of
4.8% through April&nbsp;27, 2010 on the hedged portion of the Company&#146;s
borrowings as of December&nbsp;31, 2006. The Company paid a commitment fee of
0.13% until October&nbsp;2006 and 0.10% afterwards on the unused portion of the
Revolving Credit Facility. As of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005, the Company
had letters of credit outstanding of $4.6&nbsp;million and $4.5&nbsp;million
respectively, which reduced the borrowing capacity </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">18</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-18',FILE='C:\fc\5417522144_D11055_1758917\5232-1-fm.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Feb 23 17:53 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">



<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">under the Revolving Credit
Facility. Outstanding borrowings were $495.0&nbsp;million and $390.7&nbsp;million
as of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005, respectively. Available borrowings under
the Revolving Credit Facility were $100.4&nbsp;million and $204.8&nbsp;million
as of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Revolving Credit Facility was amended in October&nbsp;2006
(the &#147;First Amendment&#148;). The First Amendment reduced applicable margins and
fees under the Revolving Credit Facility as determined by debt ratings issued
by third-party rating agencies. Based upon current third party debt ratings,
the interest rate on U.S. dollar denominated borrowings was reduced by 0.23%
from the then current rate of LIBOR plus 0.63%. In addition, the commitment fee
on the unused portion of the Revolving Credit Facility was reduced from 0.13%
to 0.10%. No other changes were made to the revolving credit facility during
2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The borrowings under the
Revolving Credit Facility are unconditionally guaranteed by Dade Behring
Holdings,&nbsp;Inc. and certain domestic subsidiaries of Dade Behring Inc. The
borrower&#146;s and guarantors&#146; obligations are currently unsecured based upon third
party debt ratings. The Revolving Credit Facility also contains restrictive
financial covenants requiring the Company to maintain certain leverage and
interest coverage ratios. The Company is in compliance with its financial
covenants as of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Short-Term Credit
Facility</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;2006, the
Company entered into a short-term credit facility agreement with Banca
Nazionale del Lavoro S.p.A., New York Branch (&#147;BNL&#148;). The $15&nbsp;million
uncommitted and unsecured line of credit is available for short-term borrowings
up to 180&nbsp;days at an interest rate of LIBOR plus 0.38%. As of December&nbsp;31,
2006, the interest rate was 5.7% and the outstanding balance was $5.8&nbsp;million.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Senior Secured
Credit Facility</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During a portion of 2005,
the Company had a senior secured credit agreement, which consisted of term loan
and revolving credit facilities. On April&nbsp;27, 2005, the outstanding term
loan facility balance of $118.3&nbsp;million was repaid with proceeds from the
new Revolving Credit Facility discussed above. The unamortized balance of debt
issuance costs associated with the facility of $8.1&nbsp;million was
written-off and recorded as interest expense in April&nbsp;2005. No borrowings
were outstanding on the revolving credit facilities during 2005.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Senior Subordinated
Notes</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During a portion of 2005,
the Company had senior subordinated notes outstanding with a coupon of 11.91%,
which were due in 2010. In June&nbsp;2005, proceeds from the Revolving Credit
Facility were used to redeem the $275.0&nbsp;million outstanding principal
balance of the senior subordinated notes, pursuant to the make-whole redemption
provision of the bond indenture. The Company incurred a pre-tax expense of $24&nbsp;million
during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2005, in connection with the
redemption, which represented the premium paid to bondholders.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Other Credit
Facilities</font></i></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005, certain of the
Company&#146;s subsidiaries in Germany had a revolving credit facility with Dresdner
Bank AG which is renewable annually (the &#147;Dresdner Facility&#148;). As a result of
Dresdner Bank&#146;s participation in the Revolving Credit Facility, effective April&nbsp;2005,
the Dresdner Facility was amended. The borrowing capacity was reduced from </font><font face="Times New Roman">&#128;</font>30&nbsp;million
to <font face="Times New Roman">&#128;</font>10&nbsp;million,
which can be utilized in the form of cash, guarantees, or as credit lines for
derivatives trading and settlement risks. Additionally, the Dresdner Facility
is no longer secured. Effective July&nbsp;2006, the credit line was increased
to <font face="Times New Roman">&#128;</font>15&nbsp;million,
utilizable as cash advance, guarantee line or money market loan. As a result of
this amendment, the Company&#146;s commitment fee decreased from 0.5% to 0.38% on
the unused portion of the credit line related </p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">19</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-19',FILE='C:\fc\5417522144_D11055_1758917\5232-1-fm.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Feb 23 17:53 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">



<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">to cash or guarantees.
Borrowings under the Dresdner Facility are subject to a variable interest rate
of the European Overnight Indexed Average (EONIA) plus 0.63%. As of December&nbsp;31,
2006 and 2005, the interest rate was 4.32% and 3.55%, respectively, and $8.6&nbsp;million
and $0.1&nbsp;million were outstanding, respectively. Approximately $1.4&nbsp;million
and $1.1&nbsp;million were utilized for guarantee purposes as of December&nbsp;31,
2006 and 2005, respectively, which reduced the available borrowing capacity
under this facility. Effective July&nbsp;2006, one of the Company&#146;s
subsidiaries in Germany also had a short-term credit facility with Citibank
(overnight overdraft facility) subject to a variable interest rate of EONIA
plus 0.63% with a capacity of </font><font face="Times New Roman">&#128;</font>5&nbsp;million. No
borrowings were outstanding on this facility as of December&nbsp;31, 2006.
Available borrowings under all German credit facilities were $16.4&nbsp;million
and $10.6&nbsp;million as of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005, respectively.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2006
and 2005, some of the Company&#146;s non-U.S. subsidiaries, excluding the German
entities, had available credit lines from various financial institutions
totaling $59.7&nbsp;million and $45.2&nbsp;million, respectively. These credit
lines are uncommitted and principally used to provide working capital financing
for local operations. The Company had outstanding borrowings of $0.4&nbsp;million
and $0.7&nbsp;million under these credit lines and other borrowing arrangements
at December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005, respectively, at the prevailing local
market interest rates. At December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005, the Company had
guarantees outstanding of $15.4&nbsp;million and $14.2&nbsp;million,
respectively, which reduced the available borrowing capacity under these credit
lines. Available borrowings under all credit lines were $43.9&nbsp;million and
$30.3&nbsp;million as of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Aggregate

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(1)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Impact of foreign
currency translation.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Reversal of valuation
allowances to goodwill in accordance with fresh-start reporting.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Prior to emergence from bankruptcy, the Company had at
September&nbsp;30, 2002 and December&nbsp;31, 2001 net operating loss
carryforwards available in the United States for Federal income tax return
purposes of $888.3&nbsp;million and $864.2&nbsp;million (including $44.8&nbsp;million
relating to entities acquired in 1997), respectively, that expire in varying
amounts from 2006 through 2022. Loss carryforwards expiring in years 2006
through 2012 relate to entities acquired during 1997.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Upon emergence from bankruptcy, the U.S. NOL
carryforwards have been reduced as a result of the discharge of indebtedness.
Subject to certain exceptions, a debtor generally recognizes an amount of
cancellation of debt (&#147;COD&#148;) income upon satisfaction of its outstanding
indebtedness equal to the excess of (1)&nbsp;the adjusted issue price of the
indebtedness satisfied over (2)&nbsp;the sum of the issue price of any new </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">22</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-22',FILE='C:\fc\5411322954_D10967_1756447\5232-1-fo.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Feb 23 11:04 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">



<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">indebtedness issued, the
amount of cash paid and the fair market value of any other consideration,
including stock of the debtor, given in satisfaction of the indebtedness. As
discussed below, there is a bankruptcy exception to the recognition of COD
income which applies to the Company.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A debtor is not required to include COD income in
gross income if the debt discharge occurs in a Chapter&nbsp;11 Title&nbsp;11
case under the U.S. Bankruptcy Code. However, under the U.S. Internal Revenue
Code of 1986, as amended, (the &#147;Tax Code&#148;) the debtor must, as of the first day
of the next taxable year, reduce its tax attributes (in general, first its NOL
carryovers and then tax credits and capital loss carryovers and then the tax
basis of its assets) by the amount of COD income excluded from gross income by
this exception. As an exception to the order of tax attribute reduction
described above, a taxpayer can elect to reduce its tax basis in its
depreciable assets first, then its NOL carryovers and then its tax credits and
capital loss carryovers.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Since the COD income was realized in a Chapter&nbsp;11
Title&nbsp;11 case, the Company is not required to include the COD income in
taxable income, but is required to reduce the Company&#146;s NOL carryovers by the
amount of the COD income. The Company&#146;s U.S. NOL carryover as of December&nbsp;31,
2006, is $481.7&nbsp;million after the amount of COD income realized as a
result of the reorganization and subsequent utilizations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a result of the reorganization, the Company
underwent an &#147;ownership change&#148; within the meaning of section&nbsp;382 of the
Tax Code. As a consequence, after the reorganization, the Company is subject to
an annual limitation on the use of any NOL carryover and certain other tax
attributes incurred prior to the ownership change. Any unused section&nbsp;382
limitation in a given year may be carried forward, thereby increasing the
section&nbsp;382 limitation in the subsequent taxable year.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition to the U.S. NOL carryforwards, the Company
has net operating loss carryforwards available in countries outside the United
States of $88.2&nbsp;million, $106.9&nbsp;million and $128.3&nbsp;million at December&nbsp;31,
2006, 2005 and 2004, respectively, with various expiration dates.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005, the total
valuation allowance is $12.2&nbsp;million and $32.8&nbsp;million, respectively
(including net operating loss carryforwards). The realization of the deferred
tax assets requires substantial taxable income in certain jurisdictions in
future years. In assessing the realizability of the deferred tax assets, the
Company considers all currently available data, its historical U.S. GAAP and
taxable earnings and losses by jurisdiction, current financial condition,
forecast of future U.S. GAAP and taxable earnings and losses by jurisdiction
and other relevant factors. The data considered in determining the
realizability of the U.S. valuation allowance includes the tax deductions that
the Company has received or will receive related to the stock options granted
under the 2002 Management Stock Option Plan and the 2004 Incentive Compensation
Plan. Under the U.S. Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, a company is
allowed a deduction on the date of exercise equal to the difference between the
fair market value on date of exercise and the exercise price. Due to the significant
increase in the Company&#146;s share price since the issuance of certain stock
options, the Company has a significant tax deduction for stock options.
However, the Company expects future taxable income to be sufficient enough to
offset the tax deduction on the exercise of certain stock options and to
utilize net operating loss carryforwards subject to the limitation under
Internal Revenue Code section&nbsp;382. Based on the above and other positive
evidence, the company has reversed substantially all of its U.S. valuation
allowances in the third quarter of 2005. The Company believes its estimates of
future U.S. taxable income are reasonable but inherently uncertain and if its
ability to generate future U.S. taxable income necessary to realize a deferred
tax asset is materially reduced, an additional valuation allowance may be
recorded.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The reversal of U.S. valuation allowances resulted in
a reduction to goodwill, and an increase to deferred tax asset accounts and
shareholders&#146; equity. Goodwill was reduced since reduction in certain deferred
tax asset valuation allowances that existed at the date fresh-start reporting
was applied in connection with the Company&#146;s 2002 restructuring are first
credited to goodwill. The reversal of valuation </font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">reserves related to tax benefits

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition, an income tax benefit of $15.1&nbsp;million

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">For periods subsequent to December&nbsp;31, 2002, it
is management&#146;s intent to permanently reinvest earnings locally or use
available cash to pay down local debt, except for, as discussed below, certain
non-U.S. earnings that were repatriated in 2005 due to the newly enacted tax
law. Determination of the deferred tax liability related to unremitted earnings
of non-U.S. operations is not practicable.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On October&nbsp;22, 2004,
the American Jobs Creation Act (&#147;the AJCA&#148;) was signed into law. The AJCA
includes a deduction of 85% of certain non-U.S. earnings that are repatriated
in either 2004 or 2005, as defined in the AJCA. The Company completed its
evaluation of the effects of the repatriation provision. Based on this
evaluation, the Company repatriated $11.2&nbsp;million in certain non-U.S.
earnings, of which $9.2&nbsp;million qualifies for the 85% dividends received
deduction. The associated tax expense of the repatriation is $0.5&nbsp;million,
of which $0.3&nbsp;million was recognized in the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2005. Tax expense of $0.2&nbsp;million associated with repatriation was
recorded in 2004.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">10.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Shareholders&#146;
Equity</p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Shareholders&#146;
Equity</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The capitalization of the Company consists of one
class of common stock. As of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005, 82,860,364 and
88,029,061 shares were outstanding, respectively. At the annual meeting of
stockholders on May&nbsp;23, 2005, an amendment to the Company&#146;s Certificate of
Incorporation was approved, which increased the number of authorized shares of
common stock from 65,000,000 to 150,000,000.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the second quarter of 2005, the Board of
Directors approved a $0.03 per common share quarterly cash dividend plan and a
stock repurchase program of up to 5&nbsp;million shares. In February&nbsp;2006,
the Board of Directors approved an increase in the quarterly dividend from
$0.03 to $0.05 per common share and authorized an incremental 5&nbsp;million
shares to be added to the stock repurchase program. During the years ended December&nbsp;31,
2006 and 2005, the Company paid dividends of $17.2&nbsp;million and $8.0&nbsp;million,
respectively, and repurchased and 7,779,240 and 3,025,794&nbsp;shares of common
stock, respectively, under theses programs. In December&nbsp;2006, the Board of
Directors approved an incremental 5&nbsp;million shares for repurchase.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s Certificate of Incorporation includes
the authorization of Series&nbsp;A Junior Participating Preferred Stock (&#147;Preferred
Stock&#148;). The May&nbsp;23, 2005 amendment increased the number of authorized
shares of Preferred Stock from 65,000 to 150,000. No Preferred Stock shares
have been issued. Additionally, as of October&nbsp;3, 2002, the Company granted
one share purchase right (&#147;Right&#148;) for each share of new common stock, which
are described in the Rights Agreement.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">24</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Rights Agreement
provides that each Right holder may purchase 1/1000 of a share of Preferred
Stock for a price generally at a discount to the prevailing market price upon
the occurrence of certain events (&#147;triggering events&#148;). Primarily, if any
person notifies the Company of or announces publicly an intent to acquire or
acquires (with the view of controlling the Company) 15% or more of the common
shares of the Company, the right to purchase the Preferred Stock is triggered.
In the event of any merger, consolidation or other transaction in which shares
of common stock are converted or exchanged, each share of Preferred Stock will
be entitled to receive 1,000 times the amount received per share of common
stock. Each share of Preferred Stock will have 1,000 votes. Preferred Stock
holders are also entitled to preferential dividend payments and preferential
treatment in the event of liquidation, dissolution, or winding up of the Company.
However, at any time prior to the date that a person triggers the Rights as
described above, the Board of Directors can elect to redeem the outstanding
Rights for consideration equal to $0.005 per Right, subject to any applicable
adjustments. In addition, even after the date that a person triggers the Rights
as described above, but before the date on which the acquiring person acquires
50% or more of the Company&#146;s outstanding shares, the Board of Directors can
elect to exchange each outstanding Right for one share of common stock, subject
to any applicable adjustments.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Equity Compensation
Plans</font></i></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The 2004 Incentive Compensation Plan provides for the
issuance of up to 6,800,000&nbsp;shares of common stock. During 2006 and 2005,
2,361,450 and 2,124,560 stock options were granted under this plan,
respectively. Approximately one-third of these options vest and become
exercisable at the end of each of the first, second and third anniversaries of
the grant date. Vested and exercisable options expire on the earlier of (1)&nbsp;the
tenth anniversary of the date of grant, or (2)&nbsp;generally within six-months
or less after termination depending on the specific cause. Upon a change of
control as defined in the option plan, the options can be converted, cashed-out
or otherwise dealt with in accordance with the plan&#146;s provisions. Generally,
accelerated vesting of all options occurs upon a change of control. The strike
price for the options granted in 2004, 2005 and 2006 was equal to the market
price of the stock at the grant date. During 2006, the annual grant date of
stock option awards was changed from October&nbsp;3</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">rd</font>&#160;to
the seventh business day following the third quarter earnings release.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2006 and
2005, 33,020 and 9,045 restricted stock units were granted under the 2004
Incentive Compensation Plan. The 2006 grants vest either on the first
anniversary of the grant date or one-third on the first, second and third
anniversaries of the grant date. Approximately one-third of the 2005 grants
vest on the first, second and third anniversaries of the grant date. The fair
value of the restricted stock units equaled the market price of the stock on
the grant date.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s 2002 plan of reorganization included the
2002 Management Stock Option Plan and 2002 Chief Executive Officer Equity Plan,
which provided for the issuance of up to 14,117,648 stock options with
predetermined strike prices. Effective October&nbsp;3, 2002, these equity
compensation plans and the option strike prices were approved by all voting classes
of creditors and by the bankruptcy court. On October&nbsp;3, 2002, 10,188,600
stock options were granted under these plans. Additional grants of 45,200 stock
options were made during the remainder of 2002. During 2003 and 2004, grants of
3,660,584 and 284,250 stock options were made, respectively. Forfeited options
are not available for future grants. The terms for options under both plans are
substantially the same and are set forth below. For grants in 2002, forty
percent of such stock options vested 90&nbsp;days following the grant date,
with an additional 20% vesting and exercisable at the end of each of the first,
second and third anniversaries of the grant date. For grants in 2003 and 2004,
forty percent of such stock options are vested and exercisable on the grant
dates with an additional 20% vesting and becoming exercisable at the end of
each of the first, second and third anniversaries of the grant date. Vested and
exercisable options expire on the earlier of (1)&nbsp;the tenth anniversary of
the date of grant, or (2)&nbsp;generally within six-months or less after
termination depending on the specific cause. Upon a change of control (as
defined in the 2002 Management Stock Option Plan or </font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 30.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Accounting for
Stock-Based Compensation</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Prior to January&nbsp;1, 2006, the Company accounted
for its stock-based compensation plans under SFAS No.&nbsp;123, &#147;Accounting for
Stock-Based Compensation&#148; (&#147;SFAS&nbsp;123&#148;). As permitted under this standard,
compensation cost was recognized using the intrinsic value method in accordance
with Accounting Principles Board Opinion No.&nbsp;25, &#147;Accounting for Stock
Issued to Employees.&#148;&#160; On January&nbsp;1,
2006, the Company adopted SFAS No.&nbsp;123R, &#147;Share-Based Payment&#148; (&#147;SFAS&nbsp;123R&#148;)
using the modified prospective transition method. As a result of the adoption,
stock-based compensation expense recognized during the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2006, includes compensation expense for all share-based payments granted on or
prior to, but not yet vested as of December&nbsp;31, 2005, based on the grant
date fair value determined in accordance with the original provisions of SFAS&nbsp;123,
and compensation cost for all share-based payments granted on or subsequent to January&nbsp;1,
2006, based on the grant date fair value determined in accordance with the
provisions of SFAS&nbsp;123R. Prior periods were not restated to reflect the
impact of adopting the standard.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A portion of the stock options from the 2002
Management Stock Option Plan were granted to participants in 2003 and 2004 when
the market value of the Company&#146;s common stock was higher than the
predetermined strike prices. As a result, during the years ended December&nbsp;31,
2005 and 2004, the Company recognized $2.8&nbsp;million and $3.9&nbsp;million
of total stock-based compensation expense, respectively, net of income tax benefits
$1.9&nbsp;million and $2.5&nbsp;million, respectively, in accordance with
APB&nbsp;25. During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, the Company
recognized $13.5&nbsp;million of total stock-based compensation expense, net of
income tax benefits of $7.4&nbsp;million, in accordance with SFAS&nbsp;123R.
The incremental SFAS&nbsp;123R expense of $11.6&nbsp;million, net of tax
benefits of $6.1&nbsp;million, reduced basic and diluted net income per share
by $0.13 and $0.13, respectively, during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, the
components of pre-tax stock-based compensation expense consisted of $17.9&nbsp;million
for stock options, $2.6&nbsp;million for the employee stock purchase plan and
$0.4&nbsp;million for restricted stock units. In 2005, substantially all
stock-based compensation expense resulted from stock options. Total
unrecognized stock-based compensation expense as of December&nbsp;31, 2006, was
$40.5&nbsp;million, and will be recognized over a weighted average of 2.2&nbsp;years.</font></p>

during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, were $13.7&nbsp;million. Prior to
the adoption of SFAS&nbsp;123R, all tax benefits from the exercise of stock
options </font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Nonemployee
Directors&#146; Equity Compensation</font></i></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Each nonemployee director receives a grant of stock
options with a value equal to $250,000 on the grant date upon first being
appointed or elected. Accordingly, during 2005, the Company granted 16,800
stock options to a newly appointed director under the 2004 Incentive
Compensation Plan. Prior to 2006, nonemployee directors also became eligible
for a restricted stock unit award equal to the value of $65,000 on the October&nbsp;3</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">rd</font>&#160;following the completion of three years of
service and each October&nbsp;3<font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">rd</font>&#160;thereafter. The number of restricted stock
units awarded was determined annually by dividing $65,000 by the fair market
value of the Company&#146;s common stock on each October&nbsp;3<font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">rd</font>. The restricted stock units were granted
under the 2004 Incentive Compensation Plan and vest in equal installments on
the first, second and third anniversaries of the grant date. During the third
quarter of 2006, the Board of Directors approved an increase in the award value
to $95,000 and changed the vesting to the first anniversary of the grant date. The
annual grant date of awards was also changed from October&nbsp;3<font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">rd</font>&#160;to
the seventh business day following the third quarter earnings release.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;3, 2006 and October&nbsp;3, 2005, the
Company granted 13,020 and 9,045 restricted stock units, respectively, with
fair market values of $36.72 and $35.94 per share, respectively, to the
nonemployee directors.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Dade Behring
Nonemployee Directors&#146; Deferred Stock Compensation Plan allows directors to
defer fees earned and invest them in common stock units. Dividend equivalents
accrued under the plan are invested in additional common stock units. During
each of the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005, fees of
$0.2&nbsp;million were deferred as common stock units and recorded as
compensation expense and additional paid-in-capital.</font></p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-28</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-28',FILE='C:\fc\57121416560_D10967_1769504\5232-1-fq.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Feb 26 12:15 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">



<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">11.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Financial
Instruments<a name="a11_FinancialInstruments_100744"></a></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Interest Rate
Derivatives</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is subject to interest rate risk on its
long-term variable interest rate debt. The Company enters into debt obligations
primarily to support general corporate purposes, including capital expenditures
and working capital needs. To manage a portion of the exposure to interest rate
increases on outstanding debt, the Company has entered into interest rate
collar and swap agreements. These instruments have been designated as cash-flow
hedges under SFAS No.&nbsp;133, and as such, as long as the hedge is effective
and the underlying transaction is probable, the effective portion of the
changes in fair value of these contracts is recorded in accumulated other
comprehensive income (loss) until earnings are affected by the cash flows being
hedged. The fair value of the interest rate derivative agreements is the
estimated amount that the Company would pay or receive to terminate the
agreements, assuming prevailing interest rates.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In June&nbsp;2005, the Company entered into interest
rate swap agreements for a total notional amount of $200 million in order to
hedge interest risk on outstanding borrowing under the Revolving Credit
Facility. The swaps would have matured on April&nbsp;27, 2010. During the
second quarter of 2006, the Company sold these interest rate swaps for proceeds
of $9.1 million and simultaneously purchased interest rate collars (caps and
floors) for a premium of $2.5 million on the same notional amount of $200
million. </font>The Company entered into this transaction to realize
the $9.1 million value of the swaps on the balance sheet, which significantly
reduced the risk of economic loss to the Company. The collar agreements provide
the Company continued protection against interest rate risk. Under these
agreements and including the 0.40% applicable margin on the Revolving Credit
Facility, the Company will pay no less than 4.5% (floor) and no more than 5.7%
(cap) on the hedged $200 million LIBOR based borrowings.<b>  </b>The collar agreements are
designated as cash flow hedges under SFAS No.&nbsp;133 and mature concurrently
with the Company&#146;s Revolving Credit Facility on April&nbsp;27, 2010. The
proceeds from the sale of the swaps and the premium cost of the collars are
being amortized over the remaining life of the Revolving Credit Facility.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At December&nbsp;31, 2006,
the variable interest rate on $200&nbsp;million of the Company&#146;s Revolving
Credit Facility was hedged using interest rate derivative agreements. This
resulted in an average effective interest rate of 4.8% through April&nbsp;27,
2010 on the hedged portion of the Company&#146;s borrowings as of December&nbsp;31,
2006. At December&nbsp;31, 2006, the fair values of the outstanding cap and
floor agreements were an asset of $1.3&nbsp;million and a liability of
$0.8&nbsp;million, respectively. At December&nbsp;31, 2005, the variable
interest rate on $200&nbsp;million of our Revolving Credit Facility was hedged
using interest rate swap agreements, which resulted in an effective interest
rate of 4.7%. At December&nbsp;31, 2005, the fair value of the outstanding swap
agreements was an asset of $5.1&nbsp;million. No significant amounts were
recorded during 2004, 2005 or 2006 relating to hedge ineffectiveness for any of
these instruments.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Foreign Currency
Derivatives</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company operates globally with various
manufacturing and distribution facilities and material sourcing locations
around the world. As such, the Company is exposed to foreign exchange risk
since purchases and sales are made in foreign currencies. The Company is also
subject to foreign currency risk on certain short-term intercompany borrowing
arrangements denominated in foreign currencies. The intercompany borrowing
arrangements support the underlying working capital needs of the non-U.S.
subsidiaries. The gains and losses resulting from the periodic revaluation of
these borrowings are recorded to foreign exchange gain (loss).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company enters into foreign currency forward
contracts to manage exposure to exchange rate fluctuations on short-term
intercompany borrowing arrangements denominated in foreign currencies. These
contracts are economic hedges and are not designated as accounting hedges under
SFAS No.&nbsp;133. As such, gains and losses on forward contracts resulting
from revaluations are recorded to foreign </font></p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-29</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-29',FILE='C:\fc\57121416560_D10967_1769504\5232-1-fq.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Feb 26 12:15 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">



<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">exchange gain (loss) on
the statement of operations and substantially offset the gains and losses on
the hedged items in current earnings. At December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005, the
Company had foreign currency forward contracts with aggregated notional amounts
of $48.0&nbsp;million and $103.8&nbsp;million, and their fair values were
assets of $0.3&nbsp;million and $3.2&nbsp;million, respectively, which are
included in other current assets on the consolidated balance sheet.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">To manage the foreign
currency risk on sales outside of the United States, in 2006, 2005 and 2004,
the Company purchased average rate put options for various currencies with
characteristics similar to those of the underlying exposure to manage this
foreign currency exposure. The terminal value of the average rate put options
is designated as a cash-flow hedge under SFAS No.&nbsp;133, and as such, as
long as the hedge is effective and the underlying transaction is probable, the
effective portion of the changes in fair value of these contracts is recorded
in accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) until earnings are affected by
the cash flows being hedged. Any portion of the average rate put options deemed
to be ineffective is recorded in other income/loss. During 2006, 2005 and 2004,
the Company did not recognize any significant foreign exchange losses relating
to hedge ineffectiveness for these instruments. The fair value of the average
rate put options is the estimated amount that the Company would pay or receive
to terminate the agreements, assuming current foreign exchange rates. At December&nbsp;31,
2006 and 2005, the Company held average rate put options with aggregated
notional amounts of approximately $164.2&nbsp;million and $148.7&nbsp;million,
and fair values were assets of $3.2&nbsp;million and $4.4&nbsp;million,
respectively. These contracts extend through February&nbsp;2008.</font></p>

  <p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">3.4</font></p>
  </td>
  <td width="6" valign="bottom" style="padding:0pt .7pt 0pt 0pt;width:4.65pt;">
  <p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:right;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:1.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
  </td>
 </tr>
</table>

</div>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fair Value of Other
Financial Instruments</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The carrying values of cash equivalents and other
current assets and liabilities approximate their fair values at December&nbsp;31,
2006 and 2005 because of the short maturity of these instruments.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The carrying values of the
revolving credit facility of $495.0 million and $386.0&nbsp;million at December&nbsp;31,
2006 and 2005, respectively, approximated its fair values because the interest
rate is variable and based on market rates.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">12.</font></b><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Retirement
Programs<a name="a12_RetirementPrograms_100746"></a></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Pension Plans</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company maintains noncontributory defined benefit
pension plans covering substantially all employees in the United States (&#147;U.S.
Plans&#148;) and a combination of contributory and noncontributory plans in certain
non-U.S. locations (&#147;Non-U.S. Plans&#148;). The U.S. Plans&#146; benefits are based on a
cash balance formula. The Company&#146;s funding policy is to make contributions to
the trusts of the plans that meet or exceed the minimum requirements of the
Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (&#147;ERISA&#148;). The Company
typically uses a September&nbsp;30 measurement date for its plans.</font></p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-30</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='F-30',FILE='C:\fc\57121416560_D10967_1769504\5232-1-fq.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Feb 26 12:15 2007' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">



<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On December&nbsp;31, 2006, the Company adopted the
recognition and disclosure provisions of SFAS No.&nbsp;158, &#147;Employers&#146;
Accounting for Defined Benefit Pension and Other Postretirement Plans&#151;an
amendment of FASB Statements No.&nbsp;87, 88, 106 and 132(R)&#148; (&#147;SFAS 158&#148;).
SFAS 158 required the Company to recognize the funded status (i.e., the difference
between the fair value of plan assets and the projected benefit obligation) of
its benefit plans in its December&nbsp;31, 2006 consolidated balance sheet,
with a corresponding adjustment to accumulated other comprehensive income, net
of tax. The initial recognition of the funded status of the Company&#146;s benefit
plans resulted in the following changes to the Company&#146;s consolidated balance
sheet: decrease in accumulated other comprehensive income of $12.9&nbsp;million
(net of income tax benefits of $8.5 million); decrease in prepaid assets of
$0.4 million; decrease in intangible assets of $0.6 million; increase in
long-term deferred tax assets of $9.1 million; increase in long-term deferred
tax liabilities of $0.6 million; increase in accrued liabilities of $2.2
million; and increase in other liabilities of $18.2 million.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s subsidiaries in Germany participate in a
multiemployer pension plan which provides defined benefits to all employees.
Employer contributions charged to pension expense totaled $3.1 million,
$2.4&nbsp;million, and $2.2&nbsp;million during the years ended December&nbsp;31,
2006, 2005, and 2004, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In December&nbsp;2005, the Company converted one of
its non-U.S. defined benefit plans into a defined contribution plan. As a
result, a curtailment gain of $1.8&nbsp;million was recognized as a component
of net periodic benefit cost for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2005. The
assets and liabilities of the plan were settled as of December&nbsp;31, 2005,
which resulted in reductions of the benefit obligation and plan assets of
$6.7&nbsp;million and $4.2&nbsp;million, respectively.</font></p>


 <p style="margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-31</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The expected long-term
rate of return on plan assets is reviewed at least annually, taking into
account the Company&#146;s asset allocation, historical returns on the types of
assets in the trust and the current economic environment. Based on these
factors, the Company expects the plan assets will earn an average of 8.5% per
year for the U.S. Plans and 3.25% to 3.5% per year for the Non-U.S. Plans over
the long-term. </font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:18.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">F-</font><font face="Times New Roman">33</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">



<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We
generally determine the discount rate assumption by constructing a hypothetical
portfolio of investments with maturities that mirror the pension obligation.</font></p>

Company&#146;s weighted-average asset allocations by asset category were as
follows at:</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 10.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s investment
policy for the U.S. Plans is to maintain a target allocation of 65% of plan
assets in equity securities and 35% of plan assets in bond or other fixed
income securities. The investment policies for the Non-U.S. Plans vary by
country. Contributions and benefit payments are used to maintain the actual
asset allocation as close as practicable to the target allocation. Plan assets
are broadly diversified to limit the impact of losses in individual investments
on the total portfolio. Other primarily consists of cash related to a temporary
timing difference between the funding date and investment date of plan
contributions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company expects to
contribute approximately $20&nbsp;million and $3&nbsp;million to the U.S. Plans
and Non-U.S. plans, respectively, during 2007.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Estimated Future Benefit Payments<a name="EstimatedFutureBenefitPayments_023845"></a></font></b></p>

years (in millions):</font></p>

<p style="line-height:1.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 10.0pt;"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Savings Plan</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Most U.S. employees are
eligible to participate in a Company sponsored qualified 401(k) plan.
Participants may contribute up to 15% of their annual compensation, up to
certain limits, to the 401(k) plan and the Company matched the participants&#146;
contributions, up to 2% of compensation prior to 2006. Effective January&nbsp;1,
2006, Company matching contributions were increased to 3%. Matching
contributions made by the Company were $5.9&nbsp;million, $3.8&nbsp;million,
and $3.7&nbsp;million for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, 2005 and
2004, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 4.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Employee Stock Purchase Plan</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has a stock purchase plan that operates in
accordance with section&nbsp;423 of the Tax Code whereby all employees can
purchase the Company&#146;s common stock at favorable prices. Under the plan,
eligible employees are permitted to apply salary withholdings to purchase
shares of common stock at a price equal to 85% of the lower of the market value
of the stock at the beginning or end of each six-month option period ending May&nbsp;28
and November&nbsp;28. During 2006 and 2005, employees purchased 297,525 and
348,401&nbsp;shares, respectively. At December&nbsp;31, 2006, 534,672&nbsp;shares
remain available for use in the plan.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">13. Commitments and
Contingencies<a name="a13_CommitmentsAndContingencies_032136"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Legal Proceedings</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is a party in
a number of legal proceedings. Based on the advice of legal counsel, management
believes it is remote that any potential liability relative to the various
legal proceedings pending against the Company will have a material effect on
the Company&#146;s conduct of its business, its results of operations, its financial
position or its liquidity.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Indemnifications</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As permitted under
Delaware law, the Company has agreements whereby the Company indemnifies its
officers and directors for certain events or occurrences while the officer or
director is, or was serving, at the Company&#146;s request in such capacity. The
term of the indemnification period is for the officer&#146;s or director&#146;s lifetime.
The maximum potential amount of future payments the Company could be required
to make under these indemnification agreements is unlimited; however, the
Company has a directors and officers insurance policy that limits the exposure
and enables the Company to recover a portion of any future amounts paid. As a
result of the insurance policy coverage, the Company believes the estimated
fair value of these indemnification agreements is minimal. The Company has no
liabilities recorded for these agreements as of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and
2005.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Letters of Credit</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of December&nbsp;31,
2006 and 2005, the Company has letters of credit and other guarantees
outstanding of approximately $21.4 million and $19.7&nbsp;million,
respectively.</font></p>

<p style="font-style:italic;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Lease Obligations</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company leases certain facilities and equipment under operating leases expiring
at various dates. Many of these operating leases contain renewal options. The
Company has also entered into capital lease obligations. The long-term portion
is a component of other liabilities on the accompanying balance sheet. Future
minimum lease payments under noncancelable operating leases and capital leases
at December&nbsp;31, 2006 are as follows (in millions):</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">



<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 10.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-10.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">14. Business
Segment and Geographic Information<a name="a14_BusinessSegmentAndGeographicI_032140"></a></font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company derives substantially all its revenues
from manufacturing and marketing clinical diagnostic products and services. The
Company is organized functionally and is comprised of three reporting segments:
Global Customer Management (&#147;GCM&#148;)-Americas; GCM-International; and
Global Operations. GCM-Americas and GCM-International are the Company&#146;s sales,
marketing, customer training, technical support and field service
organizations. For the Company&#146;s reporting purposes, Americas includes North
and South America. The United States comprises approximately ninety percent of
the Americas segment&#146;s results. International includes sales and service
results from all other continents. Global Operations primarily includes all
manufacturing, distribution and research and development activities, which
occur in the United States and Germany, and accordingly does not recognize
significant revenues.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Earnings
before interest and income taxes (&#147;EBIT&#148;) is a primary profitability measure
used to evaluate the segments, and is thus reconciled to income before income
tax expense. Financial information by segment for the years ended December&nbsp;31,
2006, 2005 and 2004 is summarized as follows (in millions):</font></p>

headquarters, shared services centers, other expenses such as general corporate
expenses, certain intercompany transactions and eliminations.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Includes a restructuring
charge of $21.3 million recorded in 2006, which was allocated by segment as
follows: $0.4 million to GCM-Americas, $10.2 million to GCM-International and
$10.7 million to Global Operations.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt 20.0pt;text-indent:-20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(3)</font><font size="1" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Includes a charge of
$24.0 million recorded in 2005 related to the premium on the redemption of the
Company&#146;s senior subordinated notes.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 6.0pt;text-indent:20.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The United States is the Company&#146;s country of
domicile. Total sales from external customers for the U.S. were $805.9 million,
$766.3 million, and $716.9&nbsp;million for the years ended December&nbsp;31,
2006, 2005 and 2004 respectively. Total sales from external customers outside
the U.S. were $933.3 million, $891.8 million, and $842.9&nbsp;million for the
years ended December&nbsp;31, 2006, 2005, and 2004, respectively. Total
long-lived assets in the U.S. were $739.8 million and $801.7 million as of December&nbsp;31,
2006 and 2005, respectively. Total long-lived assets outside the U.S. were
$422.9 million and $404.9 million on as of December&nbsp;31, 2006 and 2005,
respectively.</font></p>

assets. Total sales from external customers for Germany were $169.3 million,

long-lived assets in Germany were $246.8 million and $248.5 million as of December&nbsp;31,
